t: What’s the Difference Between Issued and Outstanding Shares
s: May 22, 2025 - ESOPs allow employees to buy shares at a predetermined price after meeting certain conditions (vesting and exercise), while RSUs grant shares automatically upon vesting. Since these instruments do not become common shares until they are exercised (ESOPs) or vested (RSUs), they are not included in issued shares but are accounted for in the fully diluted share count to reflect potential future dilution. Outstanding shares represent the total number of shares actively held by stakeholders.
